steps.text: Dad's letters are always the same thing, all stiff and serious. You still want me to read it?
'...It is the way of the knight to protect the poor and distraught, but one should be careful with one's companions.'
'Do not let those whom you are tasked to protect suffer with you, nor should you obsess yourself with reforming the wicked and gathering the weak.'
There, he scolded you. Satisfied?
He doesn't think what we're doing is wrong, just futile.
'To save the crops, you must first plough the soil.'
Nov 30th 11:20 P.M.
Village Outside Dzwonek

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: This humble village sure has been busy these past few days, what with all the knight captains and nobles gracing us with their presence.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Isn't that so, Sir Młynar?

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: ...Give the Infected a place to stay. He's accused of instigating the riots.

steps.name: Zeno
steps.text: I-Is this the safe place that you told me about? You're handing me over to bounty hunters?

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Don't worry, you're not carrying enough cash to be worth robbing.

steps.name: Zeno
steps.text: (Nervously touches neck)

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: So if our good knight brought you here, that must mean you must know something.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Do you have family? Do you need to send them a message, tell them to flee?

steps.name: Zeno
steps.text: I, er...

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Here, pen and paper.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: As for you, Młynar... Ah, I guess you carry that sword around just to annoy folks in the Grand Knight Territory.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Since apparently you don't even need your weapon outside of the city.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: You've got a long line of people queuing up to claim your head in this place alone. Have you gotten so cocky that you thought you could take 'em all out with just a tree branch?

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: Then why aren't they doing anything? I'm standing right here.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: ...But I entrusted my sword to the campaign knights for maintenance. I'm here for a grave matter, Toland.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: I know, I know, I'm kidding, sheesh. You're picking up your weapon tomorrow, right?

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: We would've been so sad over here if you'd forgotten all about us.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: After all, there's no guarantee that you'll be coming back from your meeting with him.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Hey, don't give me that look. And don't tell me you don't suspect anything, either. Why else would you be coming to me about a 'grave matter' at this hour?

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: ...What do you know?

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Just some educated guesses, but probably not far off what you're thinking.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Why don't we give the poor man some space, though? Let him write home in peace and quiet.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: The night is deep, but the lights at the river valley factories just keep on shining. The former manor of House Paleniskos... brings back memories, doesn't it?

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: ...Pardon me, I saw smoke and thought there might be a fire. Did I disturb you?

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Nothing to worry about, I just threw a few notebooks in there. I suppose burnt leather doesn't smell too nice.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: Good to hear it was nothing serious.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: Also, the Craftsman's Guild is asking about the sword.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: ...Leave it for now. It's a shame, but the owner probably won't be back to pick it up for a while.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: Yes, sir. All the preparations are ready for the ceremony tomorrow.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Have a seat while you're here. I'd like to hear your thoughts on the operation.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: Yes, sir.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: But I'm just a junior knight. I'm not sure how useful my input could possibly be.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Don't worry. I was only a junior knight when the previous captain ordered me to infiltrate Leithanien.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: You've seen and done the most in this operation so far. Your thoughts mean more than anyone else's.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Besides, you're the Knight Primus of House Marek. You're no longer an ordinary knight.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: ...Thank you.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: House Marek prides itself on nurturing true warriors. To my shame, I have yet to have had the chance to bring glory to my family crest.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: ...Forgive me if I'm intruding, but what about you, sir? We've never heard you talk about it.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: I... true, it's something that knights would normally bring up. But the name of the house I serve has not been spoken of in years.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: I'm sorry, I shouldn't have asked.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: No worries. We're just having a chat.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: I used to live around here.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: When I was a child, Dzwonek roamed the borders, standing off against the cities of Leithanien.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Great shadows moved across the wilds when the sun was out. Children who would later become knights used to pretend they were the great heroes of history, arguing over whose wooden spear found the other first.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: That's what brings me nostalgia.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: Were the knights of the house killed in battle?

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: No. They committed treason.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: Oh...

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: I was the young son of a retainer, without status or position. When the family's collusion with Leithanien was discovered, its title was revoked by the Adeptus Sprawiedliwi Kazimierz.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: Wait, do you mean the legend of the Tenebrous Knight? The ringleader of the traitors, House Paleniskos, had gathered a dozen highly-ranked campaign knights, but they were assassinated on the night they planned to carry out their plot.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: But surely the stories are exaggerated? How could anyone defeat so many knights on their own, not to mention the casters from Leithanien?

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: The Tenebrous 'Knight,' hm...

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: I begged the young wanderer who barged into the banquet to show mercy, but no one who was party to the plot was spared.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: I suppose the whole scandal is no longer taboo, now that the dust has settled.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: ...The old captain didn't approve when I was first elected captain, remember?

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: That was because he knew I wasn't willing to give up my life to defend my house's schemes. Instead, I asked for help in trying to stop them.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: As he put it, putting justice above loyalty was a fatal flaw for a campaign knight.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: So... what do you think?

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: I only know about the incident from what you guys told me.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: When the kid brought his friends, the boys were muttering that the noble brat had a trick or two up his sleeves.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: We even made a bet.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: If the rumors that you foiled the Leithanian plot were true, then how about the rumors that the second son of House Nearl was expelled from his house by the war hero Kirill because of gambling debts?

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Oh, don't get me wrong, we also bet on when Czcibor would finally put together a flower crown for his Kuranta redhead.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: ...Or when you'd fix that bad habit of always seeing the best in people.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: What kind of person he used to be doesn't matter.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: If the contract you obtained is true, then his plot has cost the lives of countless innocents.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: It's from that little lawyer lady from the Grand Knight Territory. Probably legit.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: To tell the truth, her handing over the documents on her own was an unexpected stroke of luck.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: We were planning to spook her a little bit to get the evidence... and you almost threw a wrench into things.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: As for the documents themselves, I don't think anyone realized their importance.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: According to the sender, she was probably just playing a little legal prank. Just like how we only stopped by because we got a request for help from the village of Twierdza.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: But Czcibor was really interested in it, even going as far as to use the investigation as an excuse to take bounty hunters into custody, just to stop me from questioning her.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Which means that contract, signed by Marek Jr., has nothing to do with his house. It's all the knightclub behind him.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: ...And Gale Industries recruited the Infected as requested, manipulating the media to publicize the attacks.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: The Infected riots are the result of their machinations.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Man, I thought I was close enough to the kid that he'd at least come talk to me first. After all, my buddies definitely have surer hands than those Infected he found.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Do you think those businessmen ever stopped to think about what the campaign knights would have to gain when they're advertising their affiliates?

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: ...This is more about more than just causing a panic. They're trying to recreate how the Silverlance Pegasi entered the Grand Knight Territory not too long ago.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: A simple show of force is of no value.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: And given Dzwonek's traditions, the campaign knights don't even have to go so far to find an excuse to enter the city.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Yeah, he wouldn't need to take your sword just for something like that.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: But he did talk about wanting to take revenge for Celina.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: ...I don't owe him an explanation.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Sure, and you're not the only one he's aiming at. But I think there's a reason he set a particular time to return it.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: There's a ribbon-cutting ceremony tomorrow.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Great minds think alike.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Either everything will be over by then, and this keeps you out of it, or that's when it begins, and he wants you there for whatever reason.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Worst case scenario, it's both. Like... making you watch the Leithanian delegate die, right in front of the sculpture representing peace between the two nations.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: Enough... he shouldn't be doing this.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Wait, where are you going?

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: He shouldn't let these things get to his head, nor should he resort to these underhanded means.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: I'll talk to him.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: ...Sorry, I suppose that was a difficult question.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: I only thought that if the target happened to show up in the slums tonight, perhaps out of the naive logic we've heard from him...

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: I believe that people still capable onto such ideals should not die, even if they are often the first to fall into the maws of fate.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Heh... So why did you sign up for this operation?

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: Everyone in the knightclub is of one mind about this.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: We agree that it's time for those who are dreaming away in the safe cocoons of the cities to wake up and face the reality of our struggles and the impending threat.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: Leithanien's ambitions are obvious. Their war preparations have never halted. We should not remain idle while they're preparing to tear away the facade of peace.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: Even if this incident doesn't reignite the flames of war between Kazimierz and Leithanien, the people will remember this time of turmoil.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: They'll understand who it is that truly protects them.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Ah, that's what I said in my rallying speech, wasn't it?

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: Sorry... but we all think the same way.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: If I had to come up with something else... the battlefield is the only place knights can truly find glory.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: We're an unremarkable knightclub stationed on the outskirts, with neither military exploits or a venerable tradition to call our own.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: Most of us come from branches or retainers of the great houses, without the prestigious bloodlines needed to make it into the great knightclubs.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: But as long as we get the chance to set foot on the battlefield, I know we will prove our mettle. We will not allow mere merchants to sell our victory, nor will we cower before the enemy's guns.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: ...If only all of Kazimierz shared our conviction.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Don't say that... it's our job as knights to go to war.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Let them be weak or fearful. We fight so that they don't have to, and in so doing convince them to put faith in us.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: *cough*...

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: Is the wind blowing the smoke into your eyes? Perhaps you should move over here?

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: I'm fine.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: Is that... Captain Celina's diary that you're burning?

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Yes. I've read it enough times to have it memorized.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: But many of its records are no longer relevant. I wanted to dispose of it, lest it become our shackles in the future.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: ...You're right. We still miss her.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: You know, of course, how that conflict between the nobles disillusioned us with the Adeptus Sprawiedliwi Kazimierz.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: Hard to believe that we lost her to what began as a property dispute in a small village.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: No, it was no complicated political conflict.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Of course, I won't forget those responsible for her death either.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: They simply found an opportunity to exact revenge on us, after many years of waiting.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: We ticked off a lot of people in high places before we joined the campaign knights. They took her life as a warning to me.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: Sorry, I didn't mean to pry...

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: No, it was never something that should be left unsaid.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: We wanted to help those struggling to make ends meet under crippling taxes. Those who lost their homes to the G.C.C.'s bulldozers...

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: It's only human to feel sympathy for them.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: We've done nothing to be ashamed of. It was the nobles and merchants who colluded with the media to keep the silence, covering up their crimes.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: It was a silence that should not exist, at least not among knights.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: No knight should ever bow down to wealth and power, but there is no shame in kneeling before suffering.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: ...I'll try to keep that in mind, if I ever get a chance.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: It's easier said than done, given the current state of Kazimierz.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Most who pursue their ideals here find themselves walking not on wide roads and flat terrain, but rather stumbling along the edge of a cliff.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Those who throw themselves bravely into the abyss don't even make a sound.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: ...That's why I'm trying to bring the thunder of war to this land, and carve out a path amidst despair.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: You're going to go find him? Where? The campaign knight camp?

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: Where else?

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: I wrote to him, you know. Anything there is to say, I already did. I don't know if we can still convince him to turn back.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: ...Sitting around and watching this unfold is not an option, Toland.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: I can't stand idly by while he puts all his hopes on war. That's akin to admitting failure.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: ...Disillusionment leads to extreme solutions. It's because we understand that we're angry.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Not at him, though... at the Kazimierz that's driven us all to desperation.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: But even if you wanted to pit yourselves against the entire knightclub, and had the ability to do so... that's why he took your sword.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: There's nothing stopping me from trying to dissuade him.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: —Why do you think the hunters were so willing to follow you back then?

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: You don't have to make enemies of the campaign knights.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: And you don't have to be so reckless.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: I know what you're concerned about, of course.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: It's certainly harder for us to make a move when our brothers are still in their hands, and we could hardly expect to go head-to-head with campaign knights.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: But it's sad enough for Czcibor to have gone rogue on us. Can't you at least give me the hope that not all knights are like that?
I didn't like how my father saw things. Who decides who's the farmer, and who are the crops?
Who decides they could push crops into the earth to make it more fertile?
...No, I won't write this in the letter. A knight should not question endlessly, not without finding an answer into which he can place his trust.
But I'll always remember the questions.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: ...I mean, I won't stop you if you still want to go have a chat with him. I'll just sit here lamenting how friendships change.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: But really think about it.

steps.name: Bounty Hunter
steps.text: Boss.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Bounty Hunter
steps.text: The Leithanian noble is heading out quietly with his bodyguard.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Now?

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: They want to flee Kazimierz at this juncture? Foolish.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: They will not elude the campaign knights.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Looks like we're running out of time to talk this out.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: I came to meet up with a few new business partners. I ought to give them a heads-up before defecation encounters ventilation. It wouldn't do to get them killed in this mess.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: I have a grave matter to talk about, Toland.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: Protect the Leithanian.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: ...Deal.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Any way we choose, as long as we can delay the campaign knights, right?

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Then we do this my way, as usual.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: What about you?

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: I'm going to find Czcibor.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Hah.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: You've never turned your back on anything that you felt was right, never mind putting it on a scale.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: One last question, then.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: You're not expecting to this to end peacefully, are you?
The night wind is chilling, and the only sound in the darkness is the rushing river.
The factories stand quietly in the river valley, their massive steel silhouettes illuminated by their lights.
People still believe they can bring back the sunset, a time when blood and fire had warmth, when there was a long path ahead of them.
Now, though, there is no time to reminisce.
No time for nostalgia, or anger at all that has changed.
Młynar extends his hand.
'Give me a sword.'

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: Affirmative. Target is on the expressway towards the city exit.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: He couldn't even wait until tomorrow's ceremony... knowing full well that a diplomatic incident would ensue.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: Should we take control of the gates and stop the target from leaving?

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Is anyone else monitoring him?

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: The only people nearby are two homeless sleeping on the streets.

steps.name: Czcibor
steps.text: Commandeer the foreign visitor gate. Call it a security checkpoint.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: Yes, sir.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: ...Excuse me.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: A runner just brought urgent orders.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: They're... signed by the Grand Knight herself.

steps.name: Campaign Knight
steps.text: The entire knightclub has been ordered to withdraw from Dzwonek immediately and report to the Grand Knight Territory.
